answers.text: I would tell the assistant: always give three lines, same order — drop-off time, pallet count, damage noted — and nothing beyond that.
List time, customer, topic and outcome for each call, same order every time, then count as a follow-up anything where the outcome says it is still open.
Something about the finishing time does not sit right with me against when they start — I think that is the part worth a second look, though I could not tell you exactly why.

118 against 96 — working that through myself, that is closer to a 23% rise, not the 20% written in the note. I would want that number corrected before it goes up, since a few points either way changes how the month reads.
The second one is the one I would trust, it has 940 and 827 written out rather than just the 88%.
I would go with the second email, the numbers behind the volume increase are there. The first one just says 'better rate' with nothing to back it up.
1. No. 2. Yes. 3. No, that has not gone out yet. 4. Yes, that one is already public. 5. No.
I would keep the rates out of anything I paste in, and go careful with the confidentiality part too since it names both sides.
I would want the numbers checked against the stock sheet at some point before it is finalised.

Step four is the one I would put a gate on, since once the note is submitted automatically, it is already acted on and hard to undo. Step one still matters too, because if the invoice was misread there, that mistake is already baked into everything that follows by the time it reaches step four.
